identity.title: Herschel survey and modelling of externally-illuminated photoevaporating protoplanetary disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a unique *Herschel* survey and new ALMA observations of four externally-illuminated photoevaporating disks (a.k.a. proplyds).
Recently, coauthors of this paper have serendipitously detected intense HCO$^+$ (4-3) emission towards the 203-506 proplyd with ALMA.

question.value: What are the physical properties (density, temperature) and heating/cooling processes of the PDR in externally-illuminated photoevaporating disks (proplyds), and what mass-loss rates do they imply?

evidence.quote: What are the physical properties of this PDR (density, temperature)?
What are the key mechanisms driving the thermal balance (heating and cooling processes) and hence the photoevaporation?
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00352.S.
The observations were conducted in Band 7 with an angular resolution of 1$''$ insufficient to spatially resolve the disk.
203-506 was clearly detected in the HCO$^+$ (4-3) line.
The observations were conducted in Band 7 with an angular resolution of 1$''$ insufficient to spatially resolve the disk.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit line intensities with 1D PDR model grid

method.value: Meudon PDR code run on a grid of n_env and n_disk; best model minimises chi-square vs line intensities

evidence.quote: The best model is the one which minimizes the chi-square between observed and predicted line integrated intensities.

method.value: Supercritical (Johnstone) and subcritical (Adams) analytic prescriptions using model disk temperature and density

evidence.quote: $$\dot{M}= \mu m_H n_\mathrm{disk} c_\mathrm{S} \times 2\pi (r_\mathrm{disk} - r_\mathrm{g})^2.$$

assumptions.value: Central star 0.1 Msun (supercritical) or 1 Msun (subcritical); gamma = 7/5

evidence.quote: we used a 0.1 and 1 M$_\odot$ for the *supercritical* and *subcritical* cases respectively.

validation.value: Compared with ionisation-front rates of Henney & O'Dell

evidence.quote: to reconcile the photoevaporation rates derived from our best fit models with those derived from the observations by (cite: henney_keck_1999), one must assume that the flows are in a *supercritical* regime.

findings_qualitative.value: Proplyd disk surfaces are in a transitional regime at ~1000 K, regulated by the H/H2 transition position

evidence.quote: This implies that proplyds appear to be in the **transitional* regime* with temperatures at the disk surface close to 1000 K.

claims.hypothesis: Can proplyd FIR emission be modelled as a PDR?
claims.experiment: 1D Meudon PDR model fitted to Herschel, APEX and ALMA lines
claims.result: Most lines reproduced within a factor of a few; HCN (4-3) underpredicted
claims.finding: Disk surface densities ~1e6 cm-3, temperatures 1000-1300 K

evidence.quote: This model successfully reproduces most lines, with the exception of HCN (4-3) in 105-600.

claims.experiment: Compare model mass-loss rates to ionisation-front rates

evidence.quote: one must assume that the flows are in a *supercritical* regime.

why_this_data.value: HCO+ is a PDR tracer and 203-506 complements the sample as a silhouette proplyd

evidence.quote: Since HCO$^+$ is a PDR tracer, and given that other PDR tracers have been detected towards 203-506 (see below), we have decided to include it in our study.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Shock origin for 105-600 lines judged unlikely

evidence.quote: Altogether, we conclude that shocks are unlikely to play a major role in the observed emission.

limitations_admitted.value: 1D model cannot reproduce dense-gas tracers; unresolved observations

evidence.quote: To go further and improve the modelling of the low-$J$ CO and HCN lines would require a detailed disk model not limited to the PDR as here.
